title: Reformed concede unequal malice and unequal penalties among sins
source_text: LIX. Vicissim vero liquet ex iis quae diximus, Theologos Scholae Reformatae ultro fateri & docere inter peccata esse varios malitiae gradus, & omnia peccata non esse inter se paria: nec etiam omnia paribus poenis a Deo puniri, sed quaedam longe mitius, alia vero longe gravius in Dei judicio olim esse plectenda.
pass_a_gloss: But on the other side it is clear from what we have said that the theologians of the Reformed School freely confess and teach that among sins there are various degrees of malice, and that all sins are not equal among themselves: nor are all punished by God with equal penalties, but some far more mildly, others far more heavily, are hereafter to be punished in God’s judgment.
pass_b_english: Reformed freely grant graded malice among sins—not Stoic equality.
Penalties likewise unequal: some far milder, some far heavier at the last judgment.

choices.why: Voluntary Reformed concession before the status controversiae.
